title: Kent: Words of Estimative Probability
summary: Words hide numbers. Type a claim and move one 0–100% ruler: the number comes first and Sherman Kent's 1964 word follows, with his anchor (75% for “probable”) kept apart from his band (63–87%), and the same estimate as a natural frequency, odds and complement. Highlight the hedges in your own English and say what you meant by them; lock a number as the writer and guess it as the reader; watch clearly labelled simulated readers decode one phrase; place Kent's words yourself in a lab, then see his. Keep evidence notes with no auto-scoring, record updates as before-to-after changes, set a cost-based action threshold (unlikely is not irrelevant), and save append-only forecasts that resolve into calibration by bin, phrase and confidence, with the Brier score behind a disclosure. Cmd/Ctrl+K palette and glossary, keyboard control, shareable URLs, JSON export, and a narrated beamdswitch deck. Works offline; nothing is uploaded.
